F8.quote: Wood Quay Protests Documents related to the Wood Quay protests of 1978 and 1979, which sought to preserve the Viking site found on the planned site of Dublin Corporation's new offices. The Hunger Strikes Materials relating to the Hunger Strikes of 1980/1 in the archive.

F10.quote: The Irish Left Archive hopes to collate first-hand political reminiscences or observations from people involved in Irish Left political activity over the years. F10.claim: it hopes to collate first-hand reminiscences from people involved in Irish left activity, and asks for them

F16.quote: In 2007 the Cedar Lounge Revolution decided to initiate and host the Irish Left Online Document Archive.
F16.claim: in 2007 the Cedar Lounge Revolution initiated and hosted the Irish Left Online Document Archive

F17.quote: This was intended to be an online archive of materials relating to the Irish left with documents, leaflets, pamphlets, posters and newspapers from the latter half of the 20th century placed online in PDF format, freely accessible and easily downloadable and reproducible for those who are interested.
F17.claim: intended as an online archive of the Irish left's documents, leaflets, pamphlets, posters and newspapers of the later twentieth century, in PDF, freely accessible and reproducible
F17.lineage: what it is: an online archive of Irish left politics

F18.quote: Over the years the scope of the Irish Left Archive has grown considerably and now includes at least some sample materials from the major political formations on the island. However, large gaps still remain both chronologically and in terms of individual groups or formations.
F18.claim: its scope now includes at least some sample materials from the major formations; large gaps remain, in time and in individual groups

F19.quote: In 2013 the Irish Left Archive had grown to encompass about 300 documents and it was decided to create a new database website to make the work that went into the archive more accessible.
F19.claim: in 2013, at about 300 documents, a database website was created

F20.quote: documents continue to be posted to the CLR where the regular discussions have been invaluable in contextualising the materials and providing corrections.
F20.claim: documents continue to be posted to the CLR, whose discussions contextualise and correct them

F21.quote: It is further hoped that this site will make it easier to identify gaps in the archive’s coverage and encourage readers to donate documents and provide missing information or corrections to the existing material.
F21.claim: the site is hoped to make gaps identifiable and to draw donations and corrections

F22.quote: The rationale for the Archive is quite straightforward. Firstly it’s a good way for developing an informal but reasonably comprehensive history of the Irish left.
F22.claim: its rationale: an informal but reasonably comprehensive history of the Irish left

F23.quote: But perhaps most importantly this is intended as a general historical resource, open to all irrespective of political position. The Archive is not linked to any political party, and no judgement is made, beyond points regarding quality of production, on these documents in the accompanying texts.
F23.claim: a general historical resource open to all irrespective of position, linked to no party, making no judgement on the documents beyond quality of production

F24.quote: The Archive hopes to encompass materials from all on the left including those from Socialist, Social Democrat, Green, Marxist, Republican, Anarchist, Feminists, Trade Unions, campaigning groups, left and progressive Unionist voices and other groups on the island of Ireland, or with connections to Irish politics
F24.claim: it hopes to encompass materials from all on the left, from socialist to anarchist, feminist, trade union and progressive unionist voices, on the island or connected to Irish politics

F25.quote: But interesting or progressive noises from Fine Gael or Fianna Fáil are also of interest. Further areas include reflections upon the Irish left from organisations of the left and other ideological positions both in Ireland and outside of Ireland
F25.claim: its scope reaches beyond the left: progressive material from Fine Gael or Fianna Fáil, and reflections on the Irish left from other positions in and outside Ireland

F26.quote: The ILA was started by Ciarán Swan and the website was created by Aonghus Storey, who both maintain the project as co-curators.
F26.claim: started by Ciarán Swan, its website created by Aonghus Storey; both maintain it as co-curators

F27.quote: The Irish Left Archive is provided as a general historical resource, open to all. We aim to do so without compromising the ownership or original intent of the materials contained in it.
F27.claim: provided as a general historical resource open to all, without compromising the materials' ownership or original intent

F28.quote: In the majority of cases, the documents and posters we reproduce were intended for widespread dissemination, as a means to expose people to the ideas expressed in them, or to further awareness of the organisation which produced them. As a result, we believe our reproduction of them is in the spirit of their original production, rather than prejudicing the interests of the copyright holders. Further, other than to scan and digitize them, we do not modify the original materials.
F28.claim: the documents were made for dissemination, so reproducing them keeps to the spirit of their production; beyond scanning, the originals are not modified

F29.quote: As such, we are confident that our reproduction of these materials constitutes fair use.
F29.claim: it holds its reproduction to be fair use

F30.quote: In the case of the type of political materials contained in the archive, actual ownership can be difficult to identify. Particularly with the more informally produced documents, ownership may reside with any number of contributors (often un-attributed or pseudonymous) unless rights were specifically ceded to the organisation responsible for producing the final materials. In light of this difficulty, we feel it is reasonable to identify the organisation and the named contributors for each document.
F30.claim: ownership of political material is hard to identify, its contributors often unattributed or pseudonymous, so each document is identified by its organisation and named contributors

F31.quote: For all materials, copyright remains with the original authors. However, in most cases non-commercial re-use of the materials constitutes fair use.
F31.claim: copyright stays with the original authors; non-commercial re-use is in most cases fair use

F32.quote: we would appreciate if any re-use of materials downloaded from the ILA would acknowledge this by providing attribution (or, in the case of a website, a link back) to the ILA, as well as the original authors.
F32.claim: it asks that re-use attribute the ILA (or link back) as well as the original authors

F33.quote: We appreciate submissions of any materials that seem relevant to the scope of the archive, either in physical or digital form.
F33.claim: it takes submissions of relevant material, physical or digital

F34.quote: We add new material to the archive on a weekly basis, so donated documents won’t appear immediately on the site. This allows us time for scanning, reading and writing the accompanying commentaries for documents before they are added, and also gives time for the discussions that often provide valuable context to the materials we post.
F34.claim: new material is added weekly, after scanning, reading and a written commentary, with time for the discussions that give context

F35.quote: If files have been posted for or to other online archives previously we would appreciate if you would inform us when getting in contact. We are keen to credit others’ work or provide links where applicable.
F35.claim: it asks to be told where a file was posted before, to credit others' work

F36.quote: Many people have kindly donated documents to the archive over the years since its creation. These are greatly appreciated and have been crucial to keeping the project active and helping us to expand our coverage of the Irish Left.
F36.claim: donations have been crucial to keeping it active and to its coverage

F37.quote: Some have preferred to be acknowledged psuedonymously, and thank you also to those who have donated materials anonymously. … Irish Communist Party; Irish Socialist Network … The Socialist Party ; The Workers’ Party
F37.claim: donors include pseudonymous and anonymous donors and organisations themselves (the Irish Communist Party, the Irish Socialist Network, the Socialist Party, the Workers' Party among them)

F38.quote: A podcast looking at Left politics in Ireland from the Irish Left Archive. We talk to activists, writers, historians, politicians and others involved in Left organisations and movements about their experiences of participating in Left parties and campaigns; Left publications and political documents they’ve been involved in; and the history and development of progressive politics in Ireland.
F38.claim: a podcast from the archive: interviews with activists, writers, historians, politicians and others on their experience in Left parties, campaigns and publications

F39.quote: We also look at the role of the Irish Left Archive and similar informal projects. The podcast is hosted by Ciarán Swan and Aonghus Storey.
F39.claim: it looks at the role of the archive and similar informal projects; hosted by Ciarán Swan and Aonghus Storey

F40.quote: This episode is a round up of the Irish Left Archive project in 2025 and answers to some listener questions. Thanks as always to everyone who has supported and engaged with the archive by sending documents, speaking on the podcast, emailing, commenting, and using the site.
F40.claim: a round-up of the project in 2025, thanking those who send documents, speak, email, comment and use the site

F41.quote: Thanks also to the editorial team of Saothar, the journal of the Irish Labour History Society, for including an article on the Irish Left Archive in their 50th anniversary edition, Saothar 50.
F41.claim: an article on the archive in Saothar 50, the Irish Labour History Society's journal
